CITY OF ALHAMBRA

 NOTICE OF THE REGULAR MEETING OF THE ALHAMBRA YOUTH COMMISSION

  March 8, 2022

  (NOTICE NO. N2M22-32)

  CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) ADVISORY NOTICE
Consistent with AB 361, the Alhambra Youth Commission meeting will not be physically open to
the public, although the public may participate by video conference or teleconference.

To watch and listen to the meeting: To maximize public safety while still maintaining transparency and
public access, members of the public can participate by using Zoom Webinar as follows:
Zoom Webinar direct link:
https://us06web.zoom.us/j/88582573027?pwd=WmVQVmY3Y1BlR1A5T3dWRGltSmhPdz09

Webinar ID: 885 8257 3027, Passcode: Commission
Or by telephone by dialing 888-475-4499 (Toll Free) or 833-548-0276 (Toll Free) or 833-548-0282 (Toll
Free) or 877-853-5257 (Toll Free) or 1-253-215-8782 or 1-346-248-7799 or 1-253-215-8782 or 1-646-
558-8656 or 1-301-715-8592 or 1-312-626-6799 and entering Webinar ID: 885 8257 3027 and
Passcode: Commission. Please Note: All members of the public calling or logging into the meeting will
be muted so that the meeting can proceed.

For those wishing to speak on an agenda or non-agendized item, you have 3 options for participation:
1) Pre-register to speak: Please email Vincent Hon at rrojas@cityofalhambra.org by 5:00 p.m. prior to
the meeting with the item number you wish to speak on and the phone number you will use when
calling or the name you will use when logging into the meeting. You should then call or log into the
meeting at least 10 minutes prior to its start time. Staff will unmute you and announce you when it is
your time to speak. You will have five minutes to speak, unless that time is adjusted by the Recreation
Supervisor. If you do not have access to a computer, please call 626-570-3209 to request public
comment.

2) “Raise your hand”: For those members of the public that wish to speak but did not make a request
via email as described above, such members of the public may speak by using the “Raise Hand” function
during the public comments portion, if on Zoom. Staff will unmute you and announce you when it is your
time to speak. If participating via telephone, the Mayor will ask anyone participating by telephone if they
would like to speak after asking those on Zoom. Staff will unmute telephone callers and you may state
you wish to speak.
3) Emailed comments to be read into the record: As an alternative to speaking during the meeting,
you can email your comments to the Recreation Supervisor at rrojas@cityofalhambra.org by no later
than 5:00 p.m. on January 11, 2022 to ensure that the Recreation Supervisor has time to print the emails
prior to the beginning of the meeting. Comments will then be read into the record by the Recreation
Supervisor, with a maximum allowance of 5 minutes per individual comment, subject to the Recreation
Supervisor’s discretion. If a comment is received after 5:00 p.m. but before the conclusion of the meeting
based upon its time stamp, the comment will still be included as a part of the record of the meeting but
will not be read into the record.
Any member of the public who needs accommodations or who needs their comments translated should
email or call the Recreation Supervisor at rrojas@cityofalhambra.org or (626) 570-3209 who will use their
best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations to provide as much accessibility as possible while
also maintaining public safety.

Minutes
  Alhambra Youth Commission
  March 8, 2022

The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:16 pm on March 8, 2022 via teleconference
and video conference.

Commission Members Present: Oliva, N. Quach, J. Quach, Tran, Webster
Commission Members Absent: Andrade, Cooper, Gonzalez, Gutierrez, Hernandez, Luc, and Munson
Also present: Recreation Supervisor - Rosalyn Rojas, Director of Parks & Recreation - Michael Macias,
Deputy Director - Brie Houghton, Program Coordinator - Frank Reyes

Flag Salute
Approval of Minutes
President N. Quach moved to approve the Mintues of February 8th, 2022 Adjourned Regular Meeting.
Motioned by Webster and Seconded by Commissioner Tran the motion carried by unanimous vote.

Discussing Lunar New Year Recap, and other upcoming City Events
Commissioner Tran thought the event was very successful, a huge turn out a good way to get the youth
to come out. She enjoyed how she was able to connect with the community. Commission Webster
shares the sentiments. Stated they passed out on the Rose Parade drawing entry forms. President N.
Quach thinks the event was great and went very well. There were 40 volunteers. They had a good time
at the various booths. Recreation Supervisor Rojas thanked the Commissioners and volunteers for their
efforts and for a job well done. She said this sets the tone for the next City event. Rojas spoke on
upcoming City events the Bunny Hop Walk and Arbor Day. She shared the Youth Commission would
have a booth in addition to volunteering with the games booths. She also spoke about the Arbor Day
event and how they participated last year and how she was unsure due to school schedules would they
be able to join in this year. Commission Webster asked if there would be an opportunity for the youth
Commission to be a part of the tree planting as they did last year. Direct Mike Macias shared that the
tree planting would be Saturday, April 2, 2022, at 8:00 AM. Supervisor Rojas stated this may be how to
participate in Arbor Day and would discuss it further with President Nicolas. Commissioner Oliva
asked if they could attend the Arbor Day event or did they need to assist with setup. Supervisor Rojas
shared they could attend the event.

Discussing the status of Community Engagement with the Seniors. Tech Talk and New Ideas
President N. Quach thought Tech Talk went well. He said it was different from what he had envisioned
however he found it insightful. It does bridge the gap between older folks and younger folks. He went
on to remind the Commissioners to think of other ways how they can bridge the gap between the
generations. Supervisor Rojas asked if they had any new ideas to share regarding Senior engagement.
There was mention of anything new.
Discussion Regarding the Youth Summit – Status
President N. Quach shared he connected with John the CEO of the Alhambra Chamber of Commerce
he was interested in what the Youth Commission does and a possible partnership. Going forward John
would like to schedule an in-person meeting at the Chamber to discuss the next steps in partnering.
President N. Quach reached out to the ASB Presidents of AUSD, Alhambra High school has confirmed
their attendance and is waiting to hear back from Mark Keppel and San Gabriel High Schools. He
recommends including the Department heads in the Youth Summit. Supervisor Rojas inquired about
the Youth Summit flyer to start promoting and offered a sample City flyer. Commissioner Webster
offered to help make the flyer. Supervisor Rojas mentioned the event including survey questions for the
Youth of Alhambra to aid in establishing a theme for the summit. With the questions not available and
time being an issue she suggested the theme of mental health or education as discussed.
 President N. Quach said what's important to the youth of today is activism and advocacy specifically.
Deputy Director Houghton questioned how the proposed theme would tie in with the Department heads.
President N. Quach stated he wanted to keep the theme broad and how the youth of Alhambra want to see
change. Commissioner Oliva agreed with the theme of activism to see how City leaders are making a
change. Coordinator Reyes said he felt like the line of questioning was more of a town hall meeting and not
appropriate. Went on to state the point of the summit is to bring the youth together and hear their voices on
what their concerns are in the community. President N. Quach clarified they'd be provided the questions in
advance and how it's more about advocacy and the aspect of community and what they're currently working
on. Supervisor Rojas stated how they discussed an educational carousel format for the Summit as opposed
to a lineup of guest speakers. Commissioner Webster located the questions for the survey and felt they
needed to update them before submitting them. President N. Quach suggested they send the questions to
City staff for review for input and review them at the next Commission meeting. Commissioner Webster
suggested we establish the theme for the Summit and the questions reflect accordingly. Supervisor Rojas
suggested establishing the 2022 Summit theme and adding new questions to their existing list to present at
the event and using them as building blocks moving forward. Commissioner Webster suggested it was best
to focus on the theme of education and mental health and invite the Dream Center which provides resources
to students. President N. Quach questioned if there were any other proposed themes. Coordinator Reyes
said there's no better way to promote advocacy than to promote the Youth Commission. Deputy Director
Houghton proposes putting the themes together as Leveling Up. Commissioner Oliva suggests an advocacy
station at the summit and has potential contacts to include. Deputy Director Houghton proposes they take a
vote to determine the theme. President N. Quach takes a vote from the Commissioners, Leveling Up was
voted as the theme. Supervisor Rojas congratulates the Commission on their first Youth Summit theme. She
stresses the importance of the flyer being complete as soon as possible. Commissioner Oliva suggests
setting a deadline for the flyer to help in contacting organizations as vendors. The Commission was asked
by Supervisor Rojas to put together a list of vendors, keynote speakers, sponsors, timeline, etc. with a
deadline of March 25, 2022. President N. Quach proposes moving the event time from 9 AM-12 PM to
starting at noon. Commissioner Oliva suggests keeping the time early to help get vendors. Commissioner
Webster shared his sentiments. The time for the event was taken to a vote, it was voted in favor of the event
time being 9 AM - 12 PM. President N. Quach said as they plan this Youth Summit it stays led by the
Commission. It's great to have the input and help of the City staff, going forward the Youth Commission
should make the decisions and we continue to empower the people on the Commission

Oral Communications
No Commission Orals at this time.

Commission Orals
Commissioner Tran shared this is her last term on the Commission. She thanked everyone for the time
they've spent together. Commissioner Webster thank Commissioner Tran and congratulated her.
Commissioner Oliva echoed her sentiments and thanked the City staff for helping with timelines. President
N. Quach appreciates her and her work for District 4. He went on to state the email blast for the meeting
was sent out late and the Commission was unsure if they had a meeting. He shared that on March 19, the
was a Read Across America Event, teachers from Alahmabra would offer extra credit if they signed up to
help. Deputy Director Houghton asked if this was a Brown Act function. Director Macias clarified as long
as they did not participate as a member of the Youth Commission it was ATA.

Adjournment
President N. Quach motioned adjournedment at 7:27 PM
